faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for an 18-year-old in Australia?
faqs.a: The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage for adults at $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. For employees under 21, award-specific junior rates apply. For example, under the General Retail Industry Award, an 18-year-old may receive 70% of the adult rate, but the exact percentage depends on the award. Check your award or agreement on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, super, and deductions. Our timesheet does this calculation for you.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to junior rates?
faqs.a: Yes, casual loading of 25% is added on top of the base hourly rate, including junior rates if applicable. For example, if an 18-year-old's base rate under an award is $18.51 per hour, the casual rate would be $23.14 per hour. The loading compensates for lack of paid leave. Use our timesheet with the casual loading checkbox to see the effect.

bodyMarkdown:
## Minimum Wage for an 18-Year-Old: Hourly to Annual Pay

If you are an 18-year-old starting work or comparing a salary offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual pay is essential. This guide explains the conversion, the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax. We also show how to use our [the timesheet](/) to calculate your figures.

### The Basic Formula for Annual Pay

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula becomes:

**hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. For example, working 20 hours per week at $26.44 per hour gives annual gross pay of $27,497.60.

To see your fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38-hour week at the adult minimum wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly pay is $2,009.80 before deductions.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates for Juniors

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage for adults (21 and over) at **$26.44 per hour** from 1 July 2026. This equates to $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, the **minimum wage for an 18-year-old** is typically lower under most modern awards. Awards specify junior rates as a percentage of the adult rate, varying by age and industry.

For example, under the General Retail Industry Award, an 18-year-old may receive 70% of the adult rate, but the exact percentage depends on the award and classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award. Use our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page to find the correct rate for your situation. Remember, these are award averages, not a job median.

If you are not covered by an award, the National Minimum Wage applies, but only if you are 21 or over. For 18-year-olds without an award, the minimum wage may still be the adult rate if no junior provision exists, but this is rare. Always check your employment contract or agreement.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (sick leave, annual leave). For an adult on the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). For an 18-year-old on a junior award rate, the loading applies to that junior rate. For example, if your base rate is $18.51 per hour, the casual rate is $23.14 per hour.

Our [the timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of the base rate you enter. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – let the tool add it for you.

Superannuation (super) is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an 18-year-old earning $18.51 per hour for 38 hours a week ($36,607.76 annual base), the employer would contribute $4,392.93 in super annually (12% of $36,607.76). Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation.

For an 18-year-old earning $36,607.76 annually (junior rate example), the tax would be approximately:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $18,407.76 = $2,761.16
- Medicare levy: 2% of $36,607.76 = $732.16 (assuming no reduction)
- Total tax and Medicare: $3,493.32
- Take-home pay: $33,114.44 per year, or about $637.20 per week.

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed estimate. Note that this estimate does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and select casual loading if applicable. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super (on top), and an estimate of your weekly take-home amount. Remember the assumptions: annual pay is based on the hours you enter – we assume 38 hours per week unless you change it. The calculator respects the same rules outlined here. Check your award or agreement for your actual rates, especially for the **minimum wage 18 year old** scenario. For industry averages, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page, which uses Australian Bureau of Statistics data (full-time adult ordinary time $2,083.70 per week as of May 2026). That is an average, not a median for your job.

### Final Notes

Always verify your exact pay conditions with your employer or the Fair Work Ombudsman. The figures here are estimates based on standard rules. For more on super and packaging, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging). For hourly conversion tips, see [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).
